settings.filters.delete.open.description: The button of the section Delete filter, which asks before deleting the keyword filter.

settings.filters.delete.title.description: The question of the confirmation before a keyword filter is deleted. name is the filter's name.

settings.filters.delete.text.defaultMessage: Its words are deleted with it. This cannot be undone.
settings.filters.delete.text.description: The text of the confirmation before a keyword filter is deleted.

settings.filters.delete.confirm.description: The button of the confirmation that deletes the keyword filter; the page then goes back to the list.

settings.filters.delete.cancel.description: The button of the confirmation that keeps the keyword filter.

settings.filters.delete.failed.defaultMessage: The filter could not be deleted. Try again.
settings.filters.delete.failed.description: In the bar at the bottom of a keyword filter's form when deleting it got no answer from the server.

settings.filters.leave.title.description: The question of the confirmation that opens when the reader leaves a keyword filter's form with changes they have not saved.

settings.filters.leave.text.defaultMessage: The changes you have not saved will be lost. This cannot be undone.
settings.filters.leave.text.description: The text of the confirmation that asks whether to leave a keyword filter's form without saving.

settings.filters.leave.confirm.description: The button of the confirmation that leaves a keyword filter's form and drops the changes not saved.

settings.filters.leave.cancel.description: The button of the confirmation that stays on a keyword filter's form, with the changes as the reader left them.

settings.filters.not_found.defaultMessage: This filter does not exist. It may have been deleted.
settings.filters.not_found.description: In place of a keyword filter's form at an address that names no filter of the reader's; the link to the list follows it (settings.filters.all).

settings.filters.all.description: The link after settings.filters.not_found that leads to the list of keyword filters.

settings.filters.fact.does.defaultMessage: {action, select, warn {Folds matching posts} other {Hides matching posts}}
settings.filters.fact.does.description: A fact under a filter's name in the list of keyword filters, first on its first line: what it does to a post that holds one of its words (warn: the post shows only the filter's name and Show; hide: the post is left out). A phrase, without a full stop.

settings.filters.fact.words.description: A fact under a filter's name in the list of keyword filters, after what it does on the same line: how many words or phrases it has. Without a full stop.

settings.filters.fact.where.description: A fact under a filter's name in the list of keyword filters, first on its second line: where it applies. places is a list of settings.filters.place joined in the reader's language. A phrase, without a full stop.

settings.filters.fact.ends.description: A fact under a filter's name in the list of keyword filters, after where it applies: when it stops applying. state is never, ends (it ends on date) or ended (it ended on date and applies nowhere); date is a day (Dec 18, 2026). Without a full stop.

settings.account.status.description: A heading on the settings page Account and data, over what the moderators did to the reader's account; also the title of the page under it that lists the moderation actions on the account, the link after settings.account.action.not_found that leads there, and the button at the top of one action's page that goes back to it. A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.status.in_effect.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {A moderation action is in effect on your account} other {# moderation actions are in effect on your account}}
settings.account.status.in_effect.description: The heading of the summary at the top of the settings page Account and data while moderators' actions are in effect on the reader's account (a limit, a restriction of posting). count is how many, 1 or more. A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.status.in_effect.about.defaultMessage: {appealable, select, deadline {Account status says what each action does, why, and when it ends. You can appeal until {date}.} yes {Account status says what each action does, why, and when it ends. You can appeal an action once.} other {Account status says what each action does, why, when it ends, and where your appeal stands.}}
settings.account.status.in_effect.about.description: Under settings.account.status.in_effect: what the page Account status (settings.account.status) holds, before the button that opens it. appealable is deadline while the reader can still appeal one of the actions and the server says until when (date is the nearest last day, as the reader's locale writes a date), yes while they can and no last day is known, and anything else once every action is appealed or its time to appeal has passed.

settings.account.status.open.description: The button of the summary at the top of the settings page Account and data that opens the page Account status (settings.account.status).

settings.account.status.row.description: A row of the section Account status on the settings page Account and data, shown while no moderation action is in effect on the reader's account; it opens the page Account status, which lists the past actions and the reader's appeals.

settings.account.status.row.none.defaultMessage: No moderation action is in effect on your account.
settings.account.status.row.none.description: The line under settings.account.status.row: the state of the reader's account while no moderators' action is in effect on it.

settings.account.status.loading.description: In the section Account status of the settings page Account and data while the moderation actions on the reader's account are read from the server.

settings.account.status.failed.defaultMessage: Your account status could not be loaded.
settings.account.status.failed.description: In the section Account status of the settings page Account and data when the moderation actions on the reader's account could not be read (the network, the server); Try again follows it (settings.retry).

settings.account.actions.active.description: A heading on the settings page Account status, over the list of the moderators' actions in effect on the reader's account now. The page of an account kept out of the app says In effect (auth.status.action_active) with the same word. A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.actions.active.empty.defaultMessage: No moderation action is in effect on your account. If a moderator acts on your account, the action appears here with its reason, and you can appeal it.
settings.account.actions.active.empty.description: In place of the list Actions in effect on the settings page Account status while no moderators' action is in effect on the reader's account: the fact, what appears there, and what the reader can then do.

settings.account.actions.past.description: A heading on the settings page Account status, over the list of the moderators' actions on the reader's account that ended or were lifted. A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.actions.past.empty.defaultMessage: No past action. An action that ended or was lifted stays listed here, with your appeal and its result.
settings.account.actions.past.empty.description: In place of the list Past actions on the settings page Account status while no moderators' action on the reader's account has ended or been lifted.

settings.account.actions.more.description: The button under the list Past actions on the settings page Account status, which loads the next, older actions.

settings.account.actions.failed_more.defaultMessage: The older actions could not be loaded.
settings.account.actions.failed_more.description: Under the list Past actions on the settings page Account status when its next, older actions could not be read; Try again follows it (settings.retry).

settings.account.action.title.description: The title of the page of one moderators' action on the reader's account, under the settings page Account status: what the action does, the moderators' reason, the posts it is about, and the reader's appeal. A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.action.ends.defaultMessage: {state, select, until {Ends on {date}} expired {Ended on {date}} lifted {Lifted on {date}} other {Lasts until a moderator lifts it}}
settings.account.action.ends.description: A line of a moderators' action on the reader's account, in the lists of the settings page Account status and on the action's own page: when it ends or ended. state is until (in effect, with an end; date is the end), expired (it ended at date), lifted (a moderator lifted it at date), or anything else for an action in effect with no end. date is a date and a time as the reader's locale writes them. A line of a list: no full stop.

settings.account.action.appeal_state.defaultMessage: {state, select, open {You can appeal until {date}} open_always {You can appeal} passed {The time to appeal passed on {date}} pending {Appeal under review} upheld {Appeal reviewed: action kept} overturned {Appeal reviewed: action lifted} other {This action can no longer be appealed}}
settings.account.action.appeal_state.description: A line of a moderators' action on the reader's account, in the lists of the settings page Account status: where its appeal stands. state is open (not appealed, can be until date), open_always (can be, no last day known), passed (not appealed, the last day was date), pending (appealed, waiting for the moderators), upheld (the moderators kept the action), overturned (they lifted it), or anything else for an action that was not appealed and cannot be. The words of pending, upheld and overturned are those of the page of an account kept out of the app (auth.status.appeal_state_label: Under review, Action kept, Action lifted). A line of a list: no full stop.

settings.account.action.section.what.description: A heading on the page of one moderators' action on the reader's account (settings.account.action.title), over what the action does to the account, in the server's words, and when it was taken and ends. A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.action.section.reason.description: A heading on the page of one moderators' action on the reader's account, over the kind of reason (spam, a violation of the server's rules) and the moderators' explanation to the reader. A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.action.section.posts.description: A heading on the page of one moderators' action on the reader's account, over the reader's posts the action acted on (marked as sensitive, or deleted). A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.action.issued.description: A line under what a moderators' action does, on the action's page in the settings: when the moderators took it. date is a date and a time as the reader's locale writes them. No full stop.

settings.account.action.reason.none.defaultMessage: The moderators gave no explanation with this action.
settings.account.action.reason.none.description: Under the kind of reason of a moderators' action on the reader's account, on the action's page in the settings, when the moderators wrote no explanation to the reader.

settings.account.action.post.description: A row of the list Posts this action is about, on the page of a moderators' action in the settings: one of the reader's posts, named by when it was posted, which the row opens; the start of its text follows on the next line. date is a date and a time as the reader's locale writes them.

settings.account.action.posts.loading.description: In place of the list Posts this action is about, on the page of a moderators' action in the settings, while the posts are read from the server.

settings.account.action.posts.gone.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# post is no longer on this server, so it cannot be opened.} other {# posts are no longer on this server, so they cannot be opened.}}
settings.account.action.posts.gone.description: Under the list Posts this action is about, on the page of a moderators' action in the settings: how many of the posts the action acted on were deleted (by the action or since) and so have no page to open. count is 1 or more.

settings.account.action.not_found.defaultMessage: This moderation action is not listed on your account. Check the address.
settings.account.action.not_found.description: In place of the page of a moderators' action at an address that names no action on the reader's account; the link to the page Account status follows it (settings.account.status).

settings.account.appeal.description: A heading on the page of one moderators' action on the reader's account, over the form in which the reader asks the moderators to reconsider the action, or over the appeal they sent and its result. A heading: no full stop.

settings.account.appeal.about.defaultMessage: {deadline, select, yes {You can appeal this action once, until {date}, and you cannot change your appeal after you send it. A moderator reads it and decides.} other {You can appeal this action once, and you cannot change your appeal after you send it. A moderator reads it and decides.}}
settings.account.appeal.about.description: Under the heading Appeal on the page of a moderators' action in the settings, over the appeal form: that an action is appealed once and the appeal cannot be changed, the last moment to appeal, and who decides. deadline is yes when the server says the last moment (date, a date and a time as the reader's locale writes them), no otherwise.

settings.account.appeal.label.description: The label of the field in which the reader writes their appeal of a moderators' action on their account (why the moderators should reconsider it), on the action's page in the settings; also the label over the appeal they sent, once it is sent.

settings.account.appeal.hint.defaultMessage: Say why the moderators should reconsider this action, in up to {max, number} characters.
settings.account.appeal.hint.description: The hint of the field settings.account.appeal.label. max is the longest appeal the server takes, in characters.

settings.account.appeal.missing.defaultMessage: Write your appeal before you send it.
settings.account.appeal.missing.description: The error under the appeal field of a moderators' action, in the settings, when the reader sends it empty.

settings.account.appeal.over.defaultMessage: Shorten your appeal to {max, number} characters or fewer.
settings.account.appeal.over.description: The error under the appeal field of a moderators' action, in the settings, when what the reader wrote is longer than the server takes. max is the most characters.

settings.account.appeal.submit.description: The button at the bottom of the page of a moderators' action in the settings that sends the reader's appeal to the moderators. The page of an account kept out of the app says the same (auth.status.appeal_submit).

settings.account.appeal.not_sent.defaultMessage: {reason, select, field {The appeal was not sent. Check the field marked above.} other {The appeal could not be sent. Check your connection and try again.}}
settings.account.appeal.not_sent.description: In the bar at the bottom of the page of a moderators' action in the settings, beside Send appeal, when the appeal was not sent. reason is field when what the reader wrote was refused (what is wrong stands under the field), other when the server could not be reached or answered with nothing the app knows.

settings.account.appeal.sent.description: Said under the heading Appeal on the page of a moderators' action in the settings, right after the reader sent their appeal; where the appeal stands follows it (settings.account.appeal.state).

settings.account.appeal.refused.defaultMessage: {reason, select, appealed {You have already appealed this action, and an action can be appealed once. Your earlier appeal and where it stands are shown here.} closed {The time to appeal this action has passed, so your appeal was not sent. To reach the moderators, see the contact on {about}.} not_appealable {This action can no longer be appealed, so your appeal was not sent. To reach the moderators, see the contact on {about}.} other {This action is no longer listed on your account, so your appeal was not sent. Go back to Account status to see the actions on your account.}}
settings.account.appeal.refused.description: Said under the heading Appeal on the page of a moderators' action in the settings when the server refused the appeal the reader sent; the form is then gone. reason is appealed (the action was appealed already, from another browser; that appeal then shows on the page), closed (the last moment to appeal has passed), not_appealable (the action cannot be appealed any more), or other (the action is not on the account any more). about is the link to the server's About page, whose words are settings.account.appeal.about_page; Account status is settings.account.status.

settings.account.appeal.about_page.description: The words of the link in settings.account.appeal.refused (its about) that leads to the server's About page (app.footer_about), where the server's contact is. It stands inside a sentence: no capital, no full stop.

settings.account.appeal.unsent.description: The label over the text of the appeal the reader wrote, on the page of a moderators' action in the settings, after the server refused the appeal because the action can no longer be appealed: the text stays to be read and copied.

settings.account.appeal.unsent.about.defaultMessage: Copy it if you want to send it to the moderators another way. It is not kept after you leave this page.
settings.account.appeal.unsent.about.description: Under the text of the appeal that was not sent (settings.account.appeal.unsent): what the reader can do with it, and that it is gone once they leave the page.

settings.account.appeal.state.defaultMessage: {state, select, pending {Your appeal is waiting for a moderator's review. You will be notified of the result.} upheld {A moderator reviewed your appeal and kept the action.} overturned {A moderator reviewed your appeal and lifted the action.} other {You appealed this action.}}
settings.account.appeal.state.description: Under the heading Appeal on the page of a moderators' action in the settings, once the reader appealed it: where the appeal stands, read alone when the page is opened later. state is pending, upheld (the action stays), or overturned (the action is lifted). The first sentence of each is the page of an account kept out of the app's (server:auth.status.appeal_state).

settings.account.appeal.sent_on.description: A line under where the reader's appeal of a moderators' action stands, on the action's page in the settings: when they sent it. date is a date and a time as the reader's locale writes them. No full stop.

settings.account.appeal.decided_on.description: A line under settings.account.appeal.sent_on, once the moderators decided the reader's appeal: when they did. date is a date and a time as the reader's locale writes them. No full stop.

settings.account.appeal.answer.description: The label over the moderators' explanation of their decision on the reader's appeal, on the page of a moderators' action in the settings. The page of an account kept out of the app says the same (auth.status.appeal_answer).

settings.account.appeal.closed.defaultMessage: {deadline, select, yes {You did not appeal this action, and the time to appeal passed on {date}.} other {This action can no longer be appealed.}}
settings.account.appeal.closed.description: Under the heading Appeal on the page of a moderators' action in the settings, when the reader did not appeal the action and no longer can. deadline is yes when the last moment to appeal is known and has passed (date, a date and a time as the reader's locale writes them), no otherwise.

settings.account.appeal.leave.title.description: The question of the confirmation that opens when the reader leaves the page of a moderators' action with an appeal they wrote and did not send.

settings.account.appeal.leave.text.defaultMessage: What you wrote will be lost. This cannot be undone.
settings.account.appeal.leave.text.description: The text of the confirmation that asks whether to leave the page of a moderators' action without sending the appeal written there.

settings.account.appeal.leave.confirm.description: The button of the confirmation that leaves the page of a moderators' action and drops the appeal the reader wrote and did not send.

settings.account.appeal.leave.cancel.description: The button of the confirmation that stays on the page of a moderators' action, with the appeal as the reader wrote it.
